core_obligations: Direction (1) => (2): assuming X geometrically reduced at x, let k'/k be a finite purely inseparable extension; the spectrum of O_{X,x} tensor_k k' is the same as that of O_{X,x}, hence it is local, there is a unique point x' over x and O_{X_{k'},x'} is that tensor product; reducedness of that ring for all such k' then gives geometric reducedness of O_{X,x} by the purely inseparable criterion (proof lines 371-383).

Direction (2) => (1): assuming O_{X,x} geometrically reduced over k, let k'/k be an arbitrary field extension; surjectivity of Spec(k') -> Spec(k) makes X_{k'} -> X surjective, and for any point x' over x the local ring O_{X_{k'},x'} is a localisation of O_{X,x} tensor_k k', hence reduced, which is geometric reducedness of X at x (proof lines 386-394).

Note that the two directions use different extensions: the first only needs finite purely inseparable k'/k together with the criterion for them, while the second must handle an arbitrary k'/k and uses surjectivity plus localisation of the tensor product.
proof_roadmap: For (1) => (2), pass to finite purely inseparable k'/k and identify the local ring of the base change with O_{X,x} tensor_k k' (proof lines 371-380).
Conclude (2) from the purely inseparable criterion for geometric reducedness of a ring (proof lines 381-383).
For (2) => (1), take an arbitrary k'/k, use surjectivity of X_{k'} -> X and the localisation description of the local rings of the base change to get reducedness there (proof lines 386-394).
difficulty_reason: The lemma, whose slogan is that geometric reducedness can be checked on local rings, identifies geometric reducedness of X at a point x with geometric reducedness over k of the local ring O_{X,x} (statement lines 355-367). The proof works in two directions that use genuinely different tools: for (1) => (2) one restricts to finite purely inseparable extensions, where Spec of the tensor product has the same spectrum and the base change has a unique point over x, and then applies the purely inseparable criterion for rings; for (2) => (1) one takes an arbitrary field extension and uses surjectivity of the base change together with the description of the local rings of X_{k'} as localisations of O_{X,x} tensor_k k' (proof lines 371-394). The step a reader cannot supply routinely is the identification of the local ring of the base change in the second direction, since it is a localisation rather than the tensor product itself. The claim is H2.
